definition: Successive discrimination is a simple visual Go/No-go discrimination task used to study response control. In this context, it measures how well someone can distinguish when to respond and when to withhold a response, reflecting attentional and behavioral inhibition processes.

reasons: The definition shifts the test from the mouse models described in the packet to “someone,” which is unsupported and changes the subject of measurement.

It presents the task as a general human measure of response control, attentional control, and behavioral inhibition without making clear that the packet describes it as a modified Go/No-go assay used in Huntington’s disease mouse models.
“Simple visual Go/No-go discrimination task” is broadly consistent with the article title, but the rest of the definition adds unsupported generalization about what the task measures in people.
The definition generalizes to “someone” (implying applicability to humans in general), while the packet only describes the task in mouse models of Huntington’s disease.

The packet supports that the Go/No-go successive discrimination task assesses response inhibition/attentional and/or behavioral inhibition processes, but it does not explicitly define “successive discrimination” as a standalone construct outside of this specific task context.
